about.title: A data platform and AI engineering firm
about.description: ISTech sells outcomes, not hours. Every engagement is a package with a fixed scope, a fixed price and a written deliverable. Work runs async by default: one kickoff call, one written update a week, one handover call. Founded in 2023 and led by Rafael Ignaulin, Founder and Principal.

cards.title: Databricks cost and reliability audit
cards.for: Teams on Databricks or Spark whose compute bill grows faster than their data, or whose jobs fail too often.
cards.description: We review your 10 most expensive or least reliable jobs and deliver a written report with every finding ranked by expected saving and effort, plus a fixed price to implement the top fixes. If day one shows no credible saving, you pay nothing. The fee is credited toward the fixes if you sign within 30 days.

cards.title: Analytics serving layer
cards.for: Teams where every dashboard has its own aggregate table and the numbers disagree.
cards.description: One multi-grain table with a documented metric catalog, data-quality checks on the build, and up to 3 dashboards migrated to it.

cards.title: Analytics agent pilot
cards.for: Teams that want people to ask data questions in plain language without trusting a chatbot blindly.
cards.description: A natural-language to SQL agent on your warehouse for one domain, with confidence scoring against validated questions, low-confidence alerts, and tracing and feedback in MLflow. Optional MCP server so engineers query the same data from their IDE.

cards.title: Pipeline automation sprint
cards.for: A recurring report or process still done by hand in spreadsheets.
cards.description: That process turned into an orchestrated pipeline on Airflow or Databricks Workflows, with data-quality checks and alerting.

cards.title: Retainer
cards.for: Clients who finished a package and want ongoing help.
cards.description: A fixed monthly block of hours, used async for reviews, fixes and architecture questions. No on-call, no fixed meeting schedule.

results.title: Selected results
results.description: Anonymized work from our engagements. We never name clients.

items.title: Fewer data reads on a daily Spark job
items.description: A daily job scanned multiple terabytes per run, mostly small event files it never used. We fixed partition and column pruning and reshaped the read path around how the job filters. It now reads 98% less data per run.

items.title: A/B test reporting, automated
items.description: Every experiment readout was assembled by hand in spreadsheets. We built an Airflow pipeline that computes the metrics and statistical tests from declarative config and publishes the readout. Same method on every test, hours instead of weeks.

items.title: One multi-grain table instead of many aggregates
items.description: Each dashboard had its own aggregate table and the numbers disagreed. One table built with Spark GROUPING SETS and ROLLUP now holds every grain the consumers need. Other teams adopted the pattern.

items.title: An analytics agent that scores its own confidence
items.description: Plain-language questions turned into SQL against the lakehouse, with each answer checked against validated questions by an LLM judge. Low-confidence answers are flagged, every answer is traced in MLflow, and an MCP server exposes the same data inside engineers' IDEs. In production for an enterprise client.

items.title: Customer segmentation platform
items.description: A medallion lakehouse on S3 and Delta Lake with CDC ingestion through Kafka, data quality as code that aborts bad loads, and a near-real-time update path between batch cycles. It serves 45M+ customers.

mission.title: Fix the platform, then add AI
mission.description: Data platforms tend to cost more and break more every quarter, and an AI agent built on top inherits every flaw underneath. We fix the platform first, then build agents that say when they are not sure. Every package ends with something running in production and a runbook your team can follow.
